title: P3E10 Batched Catalog Validation And Store Ownership
summary: Measure fewer catalog round trips while preserving per-lease database admission and keeping pool/session/schema responsibilities out of domain methods.
invariants: Same schema 011 and unchanged SQL migration checksums; no DDL or wire schema upgrade for this refactor.
Role and migration admission still precede structural checks; deployment pin is checked before the domain operation.
Each lease executes current database checks. Static cached data is compiled SQL and expected metadata, never an observed green result or TTL.
Failed validation discards its reserved connection and releases pool capacity. Domain transaction and lifecycle semantics remain unchanged.
Historical workspace unsupported-schema error spelling is retained; batching does not silently revise its API error.
No alternate serial production path, new third-party dependency, observer/consumer/global skill change or remote transport installation.

ownership.domain: store.cpp retains project/audit request behavior and Store operation dispatch. Dedicated domain stores are unchanged except schema-check extraction.
ownership.pool: store_pool.h/cpp owns exclusive leases, bounded waiting, connection replacement and the shared session lifecycle fence.
ownership.session: store_session.cpp owns connection configuration, runtime database/role checks and deployment identity admission.
ownership.schema: store_schema.cpp owns embedded migration history, explicit migration/recovery entrypoints and composition of schema validators. Domain validators register their own predicates and expected fields.
ownership.batch: SchemaChecks owns at most 32 constant queries with pure result validators. It queues through libpqxx pipeline, retrieves in order and drains/detaches before invoking validators. Missing relation/column/index/schema SQLSTATEs fail as schema-unsupported; connection/timeout errors are not disguised as a successful schema check.

limits: Development-only Server, no stable release or consumer cutover.
No new off-loopback, TLS, remote host, power-loss or zero-downtime migration proof.
Audit load seeds 16384 synthetic rows; Observer load uses 4096 submissions; default recovery uses registry size 1, not maximum-size recovery certification.

Broad development Core retrieval was rerun and remains 23/29 cases and 46/54 queries, report build/p3e10-self-eval.json. The inherited stable release metadata gate rejects dev.9 and was not rerun in this Store-only slice. Focused companion success does not waive those release debts.
